course.title: Atomic – Cambridge Lower Secondary Mathematics — Stage 8

unit.title: Collecting Data
unit.blurb: Planning a statistical investigation: types of data, questionnaires, data-collection sheets, populations and samples.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Plan an investigation: choose the data to collect, classify data, and design questionnaires and data-collection sheets.

O2.t: Understand populations and samples, choose a sample size and recognise how sampling can introduce bias.

p: **Categorical** data are words or groups (favourite fruit, eye colour). **Discrete** data are counted (number of pets). **Continuous** data are measured (height, time, mass).
**Primary** data you collect yourself; **secondary** data was collected by someone else (a website, a report).
Ask one thing at a time, in clear, neutral words.
Give a time frame ('in the last week').
Use response boxes that do not overlap and cover every possible answer.

lesson.q: What is wrong with these boxes for 'How many hours of TV did you watch yesterday?': 0–1, 1–2, 2–3?
steps: there is no box for more than 3 hours
lesson.a: Use 0 to less than 1, 1 to less than 2, 2 to less than 3, 3 or more.

p: 'Don't you agree that homework is boring?' pushes people towards one answer. Ask 'What do you think about homework?' instead.

p: The **population** is the whole group you want to find out about. A **sample** is the smaller group you actually ask.
A **random sample** gives everyone the same chance of being picked. A bigger sample usually gives more **reliable** results, but takes longer and costs more.

lesson.q: To find out how students get to school, Mia asks 20 students at the bus stop. Why is this biased?
steps: everyone at the bus stop is likely to take the bus
the sample does not represent all students
